## Summary
- Replace `prepublishOnly` with `prepack` so the TypeScript build runs whenever a package tarball is created—not only on `npm publish`.
- `dist/` is gitignored, so previously only a full publish ran the build. Bare `npm pack` shipped a 2-file tarball (package.json + README) without compiled output.
- `prepack` runs for `npm pack`, `npm publish`, and git/URL installs, so consumers get a usable package. release-please publish still works because publish also triggers `prepack`.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run lint && npm test`
- [ ] Optionally confirm `npm pack` produces a tarball that includes `dist/` (more than the previous 2-file package)


Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

## Context

Found empirically during the #987 review: with the build wired to `prepublishOnly` and `dist/` git-ignored, a bare `npm pack` produced an installable-but-nonfunctional 2-file tarball (8.9 kB: `package.json` + README, no `dist/`). Beyond git installs, this is a footgun for contributors packing tarballs to test PRs — a dist-less tarball silently leaves `npx` resolving whatever version is in local `node_modules`, which contributed to the retest confusion on #726/#987.

body:
Second of the three-part scope (engine → **discovery redesign** → landing page). Builds the real `/discover` surface on top of the engine upgrade, then extends it per follow-up feedback.

> **Stacked on #21.** This PR's base is `claude/wavr-engine-upgrade`; merge **#21 first**, then this. GitHub will retarget it to `main` automatically once #21 lands.

## `/discover` — the exploration surface (Nothing-brand identity)
- **For-You hero** — the payoff of the app: an editorial spotlight for the one show the crowd's discussion/ratings say is worth your time, so you don't have to research it yourself. Human "why we picked this", rating evidence, big **▶ Play the talked-about bit**, a **Shuffle** for a fresh pick, Signal-Red glow + a tiny equalizer — all reduced-motion safe.
- **One-click middle-clip play** — plays a random section of the *middle* of a show's most-discussed episode (pure `middleFraction()` + a `startFraction` seek resolved against the CDN's real duration, so it lands on real content even when RSS omits a length — never intros/ads).
- **Per-show episode lists** — open any show to see its episodes ranked discussion → rating → recency, each with an honest `basis` label.
- Layout: **Hero → Charts → ranked list → "because you saved" rails → topic-lensed trending**.

## Charts — ranked by the crowd, not us
- **中文播客榜** — top Chinese podcasts. Reliability-first: base pool is Apple's **CN** storefront chart (as reliable as the Global board), with **xyzrank.com** layered on best-effort (小宇宙 subscriber/play/comment stats drive ordering; its non-Apple shows are resolved in). xyzrank 403s bare server-side fetches, so it's strictly optional — the board never goes empty.
- **Global** — `topPicks` (no seeds) ranks the Apple chart + Podcast Index trending through **Reddit discussion + Listen Score**, leading each row with its strongest human phrase.
- One tabbed block placed **high** on the page; auto-focuses whichever board has data.

## Language-matched recommendations
Pure `detectLang()` (script-based) filters `similar` + `top-picks` candidates to the seed's language — search **故事FM** and you get Chinese neighbours from 小宇宙 / 中文播客榜 discussion signals, not the English chart. CJK seeds also pull the matching Apple storefront (cn/jp/kr) to widen the same-language pool; graceful fallback keeps the pool non-empty.

## Show detail — top episodes
The show page now lists the show's own episodes ranked top→bottom, each playable from its middle.

## Portability — OPML import + export
- **Export** the Library (saved shows + queued episodes' parent feeds, deduped) to an `.opml` for Pocket Casts / Overcast / AntennaPod.
- **Import** a subscription list from any podcast app: resolves each feed to a catalog show and saves it — signed-in, saves land in Supabase and **sync to every device on their own**.
- Pure `buildOpml()` / `parseOpml()` (round-trip tested).

## Branding
Signal Red **#FF3B30** is now the single app accent (both themes); `/discover` added to the nav.

## Checks
`tsc` + lint clean · **101 unit tests** (language, opml round-trip, middle-clip) · build clean (routes: `charts/chinese`, `charts/global`, `episodes-ranked`) · **10/10 e2e** (hero, both chart tabs, detail episodes, import/export).

author: petar-djukic
body:
Generalizes the chatbot turn's single `rag_query` to sequential fan-out over the declared RAG clients (srd014 R3). After embed, the turn queries `rag_query0` then `rag_query1`, each threading the one embedding via command-state `$from(embed_query)`; `rag_merge` (#354) combines the results distance-ordered with per-RAG tags; `compose` renders from the merged chunks.

## Design
- **Machine**: `Embedding → Retrieving0 → Retrieving1 → Merging → Composing`. A RAG query `CommandError` routes to the next RAG state (degraded), not `Failed`.
- **Declarations**: `rag_query0`/`rag_query1` return documents, distances, `embedding_model`; `rag_merge` drops a failed RAG (degraded) or an embedding mismatch (excluded), tags + distance-orders + caps; `compose` reads `$from(rag_merge).mapped.documents`.
- **rest.yaml**: `rag0`/`rag1` clients (18085, 18095), distinct operation names, distances + embedding_model mapped.

srd014 R3 → done. Depends on #354 (merged). Sequential is v1; concurrent fan-out is a follow-on. Degraded/excluded labels carried in the merge output for the response-metadata follow-on.

## Verified end-to-end
Live Chroma + two RAG servers over **disjoint corpora** (wind vs solar) + Ollama: a spanning question cites both RAGs tagged `[rag0]`/`[rag1]`; a stopped second RAG returns a 200 answered from the remaining RAG. `mage validate` 19 profiles, `mage audit` clean.

Closes #308

## Summary
Second slice of stabilization **surface #3** (state stored in untyped JSON bags that can drift). The controller's staleness / runner-liveness projection lives in untyped run-record metadata — `stale_running`, `stale_running_reason`, `runner_liveness`, `retryable`, `reclaimed_stale_running`, `cancelled_stale_running`. Those keys were **raw string literals scattered across ~6 files** (`records.rs`, `cancellation.rs`, `lifecycle_ops.rs`, `discovery.rs`, `loop_controller/helpers.rs`) with no single source of truth — a typo in any read or write would **silently break staleness detection**.

## Changes
- `METADATA_KEY_*` constants in `records.rs`, referenced by every read and write of these flags.
- Typed `AgentTaskRunRecord::is_stale_running()` / `stale_running_reason()` accessors; `discovery.rs` and `helpers.rs` (which hold the record) now use them instead of hand-rolled `metadata.get("stale_running")` lookups.

## Scope discipline
- **No on-disk format or state-semantics change** — same keys, same values. This removes the string-drift hazard and makes the flag surface discoverable, as a step toward eventually migrating these flags onto the typed lifecycle state.
- Deliberately left the `"stale_running_reason"` **JSON field names in diagnostic/history output payloads** raw — those are an observability schema for operators, not the record metadata flag, so they're a different concern.

## Verification (local, VPS-safe)
- `cargo check -p homeboy-agents --lib` — clean
- `reconcile_cancels_stale_running_record_without_manual_edit` and `discovery_active_marks_runner_backed_running_run_as_stale_retryable` pass **individually** (behavior-preserving).

> Note: the `agent_task_lifecycle` / `agent_task_service` tests are slow (60–90s each) and share runtime state per pre-existing #8964, so the batch times out; individual runs are the reliable signal.

## Context

The AWS-side deletes for both issues are **already done and verified this session** (read-only checks, no writes made by this PR):
- `aws lambda get-function-configuration email-subscriber --region us-west-2` → `ResourceNotFoundException` (the stale us-west-2 twin is gone)

## #1228 — orphan-triage region blindness

**The bug:** the remediation agent's shadow-mode triage dismissed the drift sentinel's one real catch (`email-subscriber` live-in-us-west-2, orphaned) as `"FALSE POSITIVE — defined in web_stack.py"` — true that the name is defined there, but `web_stack.py` (`LifePlatformWeb`) deploys to **us-east-1**, a different region than where the sentinel found the live orphan. The dismissal never checked which region the defining stack targets.

Note: `deploy/drift_sentinel.py::check_orphan_functions` itself was already region-scoped correctly (it only compares live-in-`REGION` Lambdas against region-local stacks' CFN resources) — the bug was entirely in how the agent's shadow-mode LLM triage read the signal afterward, treating "the name exists somewhere in the repo" as sufficient to clear a same-region live orphan.

**The fix:**
- New section in `docs/REMEDIATION_TAXONOMY.md` (**"Infra drift signals — `orphan_functions` triage is REGION-AWARE (#1228)"**): a hard rule that a function name found in ANY `cdk/stacks/*.py` file is NOT grounds for Bucket D (stale/false-positive) unless that stack's deploy region (per the `STACKS` mapping in `deploy/drift_sentinel.py`) matches the orphan's region. Points the agent at the exact lookup steps and forbids the cross-region dismissal explicitly.
- This taxonomy doc is inlined into every triage run via `remediation/agent.py::build_prompt()` — so the rule reaches the agent the same way every other taxonomy rule does.

**Regression guard (proven RED pre-fix):** `tests/test_remediation_agent.py`:
- `test_build_prompt_carries_region_aware_orphan_triage_rule` — drives the REAL `build_prompt()` code path with a synthetic `orphan_functions` signal and asserts the assembled prompt text carries the region-aware rule (mentions "region", "cross-region"/"different region", "false positive", and traces to `#1228`).
- `test_taxonomy_forbids_cross_region_false_positive_dismissal` — pins the rubric doc itself states the rule (points at the `STACKS` mapping, says "never"/"Bucket D").

Verified RED against the pre-fix tree (`git stash` the taxonomy doc change, re-run):
```

FAILED tests/test_remediation_agent.py::test_taxonomy_forbids_cross_region_false_positive_dismissal
```
Both PASS on the fixed tree.

---

## #1257 — EventBridge rule parity

**(a) docstring/CDK-cron alignment** — already landed via PR #1362 (merged, `Refs #1257`); `lambdas/web/subscriber_onboarding_lambda.py`'s docstring now states CDK's authoritative `cron(5 17)`, guarded by `test_onboarding_docstring_matches_cdk_schedule`. Nothing further needed here.

**(b) Regression guard — new I24** in `tests/test_integration_aws.py`:
- `_cdk_scheduled_lambda_names()` — statically discovers every Lambda `function_name` CDK associates with an EventBridge schedule by parsing `cdk/stacks/*.py` (same precedent as `deploy/sync_doc_metadata.py`'s AST-based lambda/alarm counters — dependency-free, no `npx cdk synth`/Node toolchain needed, and the declarations ARE what synth renders into `AWS::Events::Rule` resources). Recognizes both load-bearing patterns: the `create_platform_lambda(schedule=...)` shortcut, and the documented "manual `events.Rule` escape hatch" (`operational_stack.py`) for ships-disabled/staggered second schedules. Handles f-string cron values (Whoop's `INGEST_HOURLY`-derived schedule) and module-level constant `function_name=` (MCP's `WARMER_FUNCTION_NAME`).
- `test_i24_eventbridge_rule_lambda_targets_are_cdk_managed` — for every **ENABLED** live EventBridge rule targeting a life-platform Lambda, asserts the target resolves to a CDK-scheduled name or an explicit `EVENTBRIDGE_RULE_EXEMPTIONS` entry (empty today — no legitimate exceptions). Wired into `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml`'s post-deploy job right after I23 (needs live AWS creds — same pattern as I1/I6, self-skips without creds).
- **Offline, dependency-free proof** (runs in the main CI "Unit Tests" job, unlike I24 itself which is post-deploy-only): new `tests/test_eventbridge_rule_parity_guard.py` pins `_cdk_scheduled_lambda_names()` deterministically — asserts it finds `subscriber-onboarding` and `pipeline-health-check` (the exact #1257 offenders), resolves the f-string and module-constant edge cases, and finds the manual-rule-escape-hatch lambdas (`hevy-routine-cron`, `hevy-restamp`, `site-stats-refresh`, `dashboard-refresh`).

author: iamfatness
body:
Alpha-plan **G4 engine-off teardown fixes** — the five findings from the read-only audit against the ZoomISO deadlock rules (the reference product froze in production when teardown destroyed renderers before stopping raw data with a callback in flight). One commit per finding; targeted fixes only, no refactors.

## Findings, verdicts, fixes

### 1. Engine exit tore down the SDK before stopping raw video — CONFIRMED, FIXED
`native/zoom-engine/engine/main.cpp` exit path did heartbeat stop → `Leave()` → `share_engine.detach()` → `EngineAudio::shutdown()` → `CleanUPSDK()` and never stopped raw VIDEO. `EngineVideo` is a stack local in `main()`, so its `ParticipantSubscription` destructors (`unSubscribe()`/`destroyRenderer()`) ran AFTER `CleanUPSDK()` — the exact destroy-after-SDK-teardown order that froze ZoomISO.
**Fix:** `meeting_event.stop_raw_media("shutdown")` right after `Leave()` (raw-media off + `unsubscribe_all` across video/share/audio, mirroring the explicit audio/share teardown), plus a **bounded** (~250ms) message-pump drain so async SDK completions land on the STA thread before `CleanUPSDK()`. Never unbounded — a hung SDK must not turn exit into a hang.

### 2. `~ParticipantSubscription` renderer teardown raced the raw-frame callback — CONFIRMED, FIXED
`engine-video.cpp` destructor called `unSubscribe()`/`destroyRenderer()` with no serialization against `onRawDataFrameReceived` (SDK raw-data thread, holds `m_targets_mtx`); no stopping flag. `EngineShare` already serializes callback vs teardown under one mutex.
**Fix (stopping-flag + drain variant, deliberately NOT the hold-the-mutex variant):** the destructor sets `std::atomic<bool> m_stopping` first, then acquire+releases `m_targets_mtx` to drain any callback already inside, and only then calls `unSubscribe()`/`destroyRenderer()`. Callbacks bail on the flag at the top AND re-check it under the lock (closes the check-then-lock window). Rationale: I cannot prove `unSubscribe()`/`destroyRenderer()` never synchronously wait on a callback that takes `m_targets_mtx`; holding the mutex across those SDK calls (the literal EngineShare shape) could then deadlock. The drain pattern gives the same mutual-exclusion guarantee without a lock held across an SDK call.

### 3. `EngineVideo::m_subs` / `m_source_participants` had no mutex — CONFIRMED, FIXED
Mutated by `subscribe()/unsubscribe*/resubscribe_all()` which are reached from both the command loop and SDK meeting-status callbacks (`stop_raw_media` on DISCONNECTING/ENDED, raw-media resubscribe).
**Fix:** `m_mtx` guards container membership + `m_raw_media_active`, with the audit's build/destroy-outside-the-lock rule: `ParticipantSubscription` ctor/dtor make SDK calls (`createRenderer`/`destroyRenderer`), so unique_ptrs are moved out of the maps under the lock and destructed after release ("retired" lists), and `subscribe()` unlocks around renderer construction (destroy-before-create preserved so a participant never has two live renderers; a clash re-check after relock retires any entry a concurrent call created). This also keeps the lock re-entrancy-safe if an SDK call pumps a meeting callback on the STA thread. Lock order: `m_mtx` → `ParticipantSubscription::m_targets_mtx` (leaf), never reversed.

### 4. Leave-meeting blocked the UI thread ~1.5s — CONFIRMED, FIXED
`SettingsViewModel.LeaveZoomAsync` called `_bridge.Stop()` inline after `ConfigureAwait(true)` → `MediaCoreSupervisor.Stop` → kill-tree + `WaitForExit(1500)` under `_gate`, on the UI thread.
**Fix:** `await Task.Run(_bridge.Stop).ConfigureAwait(true)` — exactly the app-exit pattern (`MainWindow.ShutdownAsync` wraps disposal in `Task.Run`). Semantics unchanged; follow-up UI updates stay on the dispatcher.

### 5. `VirtualCameraPublisher::stop()` deleted the vcam SHM file — CONFIRMED, FIXED
`stop()` did `DeleteFileA(virtualCameraShmFilePath())`, violating the hard CLAUDE.md rule: Frame Server readers hold the file object via `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`; delete orphans them on the unlinked file → frozen frames / slate / program-slate strobing (same bug class as the delete-on-START fix that already shipped — this was the STOP side).
**Fix:** stop() only unmaps/closes handles; the writer re-opens IN PLACE on the next `start()` and the reader self-heals by path. Checked for dependents: nothing in production relied on the delete; test files delete the slot only for test isolation (unchanged). **New regression test** `VirtualCameraPublisher.StopLeavesTheShmSlotFileInPlace` drives the real publisher through `createVirtualCameraPublisher()` and asserts the slot file survives `stop()` (fails pre-fix).

## Docs
- `CLAUDE.md`: new **"Engine teardown order"** rule block (stop raw media → bounded drain → destroy renderers → `CleanUPSDK()`; callback/teardown serialization shapes; map-lock discipline; stop off the UI thread; never delete the vcam SHM in stop).
- `docs/alpha-plan.md`: G4 engine-off teardown-audit box checked with a pointer to this PR.

Watch for: UI stays responsive during leave (no ~1.5s freeze — finding 4), engine process exits cleanly every time (no hung `corevideo-zoom-engine.exe` in Task Manager — findings 1/2/3), rejoin works after each cycle.

body:
## Summary

Implements the `ClientCertificate` / `ClientCertificateManager` API for the **MRI** flavour so the pure-Ruby Bolt driver can present a client certificate during the TLS handshake (mutual TLS). This closes the `Feature:API:SSLClientCertificate` testkit gap — JRuby already advertised it via the Java driver; MRI now advertises it too.

## What's here

- **`ClientCertificate`** value object + **`ClientCertificates.of(certfile, keyfile, password = nil)`** factory.
- **`ClientCertificateManager`** — block-based; caches the last non-nil certificate so a `nil` reply means "keep the current one" (matches Java semantics). **`ClientCertificateManagers.rotating(cert)`** helper.
- **`DriverFactory#new_instance`** threads the manager into the per-connection options (previously accepted-but-ignored on MRI).
- **`TlsConfig#apply_client_certificate`** polls the manager on each connect and sets `ctx.cert` / `ctx.key`. `OpenSSL::PKey.read` handles both encrypted (password) and plain PEM keys. Polling per-connect is what makes **rotation** work — the next connection picks up a rotated cert.
- **JRuby flavour**: `ClientCertificates` / `ClientCertificateManagers` delegate to the Java factories (wrapping paths in `java.io.File`), keeping the testkit backend flavour-agnostic.
- **Backend**: flavour-agnostic `Request.client_certificate_from` + `NewClientCertificateProvider` round-trips to the frontend for cert updates (blocking, like `NewAuthTokenManager`).
- Advertise `Feature:API:SSLClientCertificate` for both flavours.

## Validation

Ran `tests.tls.test_client_certificate` locally against the MRI backend (CRuby) with the test CA trusted — **all 5 cases pass**:

- `neo4j+s` / `bolt+s` with client certificate present
- `neo4j+ssc` / `bolt+ssc` (trust-all) with and without client certificate
- `+s` / `+ssc` with certificate not present
- **client rotation** (`TestClientCertificateRotation`)

CI `testkit-tls (mri)` will exercise the `+s` schemes in the Docker environment where the test CA is imported into the trust store.

author: hawkeyexl
body:
## What & why

Interaction steps (`find`, `click`, `type`, `screenshot`, `swipe`) reached the native-app branch **only** when they carried an explicit `surface`; a surface-less step fell through to the browser path and failed in app-only or process-only contexts. [PR #671](https://github.com/doc-detective/doc-detective/pull/671) surfaced the cost — the app-testing guides had to repeat `surface: { app: … }` on every step, which the review flagged as redundant.

This makes surface routing **uniform across all three surface kinds** (browser, app, process): a surface-less step acts on the **most recently active surface**, and an explicit `surface` **switches** the active surface for the steps that follow. The router no longer cares what kind a surface is — only execution differs per kind, and there is no "passthrough to browser" default.

Implements the active-surface model already documented in [`docs/design/multi-surface-targeting.md`](docs/design/multi-surface-targeting.md), previously realized for browsers only (ADR 01019).

## How

- **One per-context MRU tracker** (`src/core/tests/activeSurface.ts`) shared by the browser session registry, the app session, and the process lanes. Activation writes ride each kind's existing path: browser `activate()`, `startAppSurface`/`ensureAppForeground`, and the `startSurface` process lane + a successful process `type`. A process registered by `runShell`/`runCode` `background:` deliberately does **not** activate.
- **One resolver, no passthrough**: `resolveTargetSurface` classifies every surface-sensitive step to a concrete `app`/`browser`/`process` handle or a clear error. `find`/`screenshot`/`swipe` on a resolved process fail with a capability error rather than silently rerouting.
- **`ensureAppForeground` fix**: desktop app references now move the active-surface pointer (the old early-return skipped the `activeApp` write), so explicit desktop references persist as active for later surface-less steps.
- **Classification follows** (`src/runtime/browserStepKeys.ts`): a surface-less interaction step no longer forces browser provisioning when the test opens or targets a non-browser surface — applied in both `isBrowserRequired` (pool sizing / driver start) and `inferRuntimeNeeds` (browser flag only; sharp/ffmpeg deps unchanged). Pure-browser specs classify byte-identically.

## Non-breaking

Pure-browser specs behave identically (the browser is always their active surface). App/process-only specs that previously errored now work — strictly additive.

**Accepted edge cases** (documented in the ADR): in a mixed spec, `goTo → startSurface { process } → surface-less find` now fails with a capability error (the process is active) instead of acting on the browser; and a surface-less step *before* any surface opens in a non-browser-signal test gets a friendly "no active surface" error. Both messages name the fix.

## Docs impact

Meaningful user-facing change → docs land with the code:
- Updated the `surface` sections of `find`/`click`/`type`/`screenshot`/`swipe`/`startSurface` action pages and the design doc's active-surface model.
- Added the `omitSurfaceForActiveApp` post-run hint (fires when a run repeatedly named one app explicitly).
- **Unblocks [PR #671](https://github.com/doc-detective/doc-detective/pull/671)'s requested change**: the four app guides can now drop the per-step `surface: { app: … }`.

## Tests

- **ADR**: [`adrs/01081-uniform-active-surface-routing.md`](adrs/01081-uniform-active-surface-routing.md) (MADR).
- **Unit** (red→green): `test/active-surface.test.js` (MRU, resolver × every reference shape/kind, handler routing incl. capability errors and explicit-persists, desktop `ensureAppForeground` activation), classification tests in `test/core-core.test.js` and `test/runtime-infer-needs.test.js`, and the hint in `test/hints.test.js`.
- **Fixtures** (PASS/SKIPPED only): `apps/active-surface.spec.json` (Windows app-only + mixed MRU flow, run green locally end-to-end), `apps/active-surface-macos.spec.json`, `process/active-surface-process.spec.json` (green locally), plus surface-less parity steps in `apps-android/android-interactions.spec.json`.
- Full suite green locally: 3941 passing (core) + 1019 passing (common), 0 failing. New module `activeSurface.ts` is 100% line/branch/function covered.

author: tannergooding
body:
Batch 3 of the v22.1.8 regressions found regenerating `terrafx.interop.windows` (follows #826 and #827).

Three independent fixes, each with a regression test (existing tests extended -- no duplicate baselines):

----------

**Namespace qualifier placed after leading cv-qualifiers** (201x across 19 Gdiplus files)

The round-1 namespace-qualification fix prepended `Ns::` to the front of the whole declarator, ignoring leading cv-qualifiers, so a `const`-pointer parameter came out as `Gdiplus::const BlurParams *` instead of `const Gdiplus::BlurParams *`. `GetNamespaceQualifiedNativeTypeName` now skips leading `const `/`volatile ` before inserting the qualifier. `NativeTypeName`-string only (no emitted-type change), but it's an incorrect type string.

----------

**Don't qualify a nested type referenced from within its own container** (12x)

The round-1 code unconditionally qualified a nested type by its container(s), so `_u_e__Union u;` was emitted as `GDI_NONREMOTE._u_e__Union u;` even from inside `GDI_NONREMOTE`. The qualification chain now stops at the reference site's shared enclosing scope, while still qualifying genuine cross-scope references.

----------

**Keep `ref readonly` on computed-pointer GUID `#define` macros** (25x in `DirectX/um/dinput/DIPROP.cs`)

#827 fixed the `#define IID_X IID_Y` property-alias form. The same `ref readonly` drop persisted for the `#define X MAKEDIPROP(n)` form (expands to `*(const GUID*)(n)`): the body emitted a `ref`-return but the return type dropped `ref readonly`, leaving a malformed by-value `Guid` return paired with a `=> ref` body. The copy-constructor `Reference` check now also matches a pointer-dereference arg, so both ref-returning `#define` GUID forms keep `ref readonly`.

----------

Full generator suite green (4165 passed), 0 warnings. Also confirmed no action needed on the neutral v22 behavior changes (coclass `IID_`->`CLSID_` reclassification, dropped defensive `unchecked`, removed `CA1508` pragma).

The self-hosted runner provisioner could pass **every** workflow step while the runner fleet silently never came up. On the last provision, 6 ephemeral runner units started but none registered Online, and the heavy trunk-dev Test job (labels `self-hosted, hetzner, linux, x64`) sat unassigned for ~2.5h.

Root cause: registration runs **inside the systemd unit on the VM** — `run-ephemeral.sh` does `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runners/registration-token` with `curl -f` under `set -euo pipefail`, then `config.sh`. A mis-scoped or expired `RUNNER_REG_PAT` makes that POST return 403/404 and abort **before** `config.sh`, so systemd `Restart=always` crash-loops all slots. None of it was visible in the run: the "start runners" step is pure `systemctl enable --now` (Type=simple returns instantly), and the Preflight only checked the PAT was **non-empty**, never its scope. So a bad PAT passed every step yet the fleet never registered.

## Fix — two guards that fail loudly in the run

- **Guard A — Preflight PAT-scope check** (before the VM is created): mint a registration token with the *exact* call `run-ephemeral.sh` makes and fail fast unless it returns **HTTP 201**. Catches a mis-scoped/expired PAT before a VM is even spent. Never prints the PAT or token.
- **Guard B — Post-enable registration verification** (after `enable --now`, **before** the SSH-key teardown): poll the GitHub runners API until at least one `hetzner` runner is **Online**; if none appear within ~4 min, dump on-box `systemctl status` / `journalctl` (best-effort, while the throwaway SSH key still exists) and fail the run.

Both derive `gh_owner`/`gh_repo` from `${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}` (matching the existing render step), use the job-level `RUNNER_REG_PAT` secret, and mirror the enable step's exact `ssh` form for the diagnostic.

Also documents the `RUNNER_REG_PAT` requirements (fine-grained; resource owner = repo owner; repo access to `madmax983/autumn`; Administration: Read+write; not expired) and the decisive manual `201` check in the runbook.

## Scope / validation

- Edits only `.github/workflows/provision-self-hosted-runner.yml` and `.github/self-hosted-ci-runners.md`. No `CHANGELOG.md`, no version bump.
- YAML parses (`python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` → OK).
- No workflow was dispatched or re-run.

## What this PR adds

A history/record ticket — `tickets/92-moderator-oauth-token-rotation.md` — capturing the diagnosis and an operational rotation runbook for the moderator's recurring forced-`/login` issue. **Documentation only; no source changes, no code enforcement** (by request).

In Claude Code 2.1, the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env token takes **precedence over** the `/login` credentials file (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`). Once the env token goes stale (expired/rotated), the CLI tries it first every session → 401 → forces `/login`; the fresh credentials each `/login` writes are then ignored next session because the stale env token still outranks them (upstream footgun: anthropics/claude-code#16238).

- **Operational rotation runbook:** `setup-token` → replace in `.env` → `./scripts/start.sh -d` (recreate) → clear stale `.credentials.json` → verify `/status`, plus a pre-rotation confirmation test

- Verified against repo state: `origin/main` still pins CC CLI 2.1.126 (`Dockerfile:128`); the running moderator is on 2.1.207 via #68 on the QRM9 line (not yet merged to `main`).

## Risky adornment prying (Build 0b, slice 6)

Completes the adornment lifecycle — **set → pry** — with the risky end you flagged when we built adornment. `pry_adornment()` is the desperate-noble-prying-gems-off-the-heirloom move: high risk, high reward. Standalone off main (adornment is merged; this reuses `perform_check` directly, no dependency on the open cut PR).

### What's in it
- **`pry_adornment(adornment, crafter, sheet, check_type, …)`** — reuses `perform_check` (the crafter's skill feeds the roll). The gem **leaves the piece either way**, so the host's `lore_value` drops by the gem's worth. Then:
  - **success** → the stone is **freed** to the pryer's inventory (holder restored);
  - **botch** → the stone **shatters** (destroyed) — the exact shatter spine as gem cutting.
  Spends the AP cost up front; returns a `PryResult` (shattered / freed gem / worth removed).

### Design notes
- **Symmetric with `adorn_item`**: adorning added the gem's worth to `lore_value`; prying removes it. `appraise()` reflects both automatically.
- **No new recipe kind**: prying takes the check config as keyword params rather than inventing a `PRY` `CraftingRecipeKind` (which would collide with the open cut PR's `GEM_CUT`). When cut merges, a shared "jeweler risky act" config can unify cut + pry.
- No models, no migration — pure service.

### Testing
- New `test_adornment_pry` — 4 tests via `force_check_outcome`: success frees the gem + drops host worth back to base, botch shatters it (gem destroyed, adornment gone) with worth still dropped, AP spent on the attempt, unaffordable-AP guard. All pass (20 with the adornment/value suites).
- `arx manage check` + `ty` clean.

### Remaining 0b
- **Domain-cron wiring** (Build-1 track) — the weekly cron calling `roll_gem_haul`, the `mine_quality` field, the minister seam (#2239), and where a mine's output accrues. This one has real economy-ownership design questions (a domain reservoir vs the player buckets, rare-find holder, minister lending) — worth a design touch before building.

body:
# Reduce CC1 runtime memory pressure and make calibration/update paths more reliable

## Summary

Centauri Carbon 1 has 128 MiB of RAM shared by Klipper, Moonraker, the UI, camera streaming, and calibration.  This series reduces steady-state memory retention, bounds the largest calibration allocations, adds a lower-RAM calibration implementation, and makes two reliability-sensitive boot/update paths deterministic:

- uStreamer uses substantially less resident memory while preserving snapshots and live video;
- Klipper and Moonraker start with lower Python and allocator overhead;
- Kalico no longer materialises input-shaper FFT intermediates for every capture window at once;
- rusty-shaper produces the same result as Classic calibration in markedly less time and with considerably more memory and swap headroom; and
- zram startup and image-owned SysV init-script refreshes are observable, bounded, and robust across updates.

The changes are deliberately split into focused commits so the kernel policy, Python runtime policy, Kalico algorithm change, and optional rusty-shaper workflow can be reviewed or reverted independently.

## Upstream dependency

This PR depends on [OpenCentauri/OpenCentauri#108](https://github.com/OpenCentauri/OpenCentauri/pull/108), which adds the GPL-3.0 rusty-shaper implementation, regression fixtures, verification gate, and documented integration examples. Merge #108 first; this Cosmos PR packages and integrates that application into the CC1 image.

## Commit series

| Commit | Change | Why it matters on CC1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `b926d5d` | `zram: make swap initialization reliable on low-memory printers` | A boot without zram is much more likely to OOM during normal service load or calibration. |
| `764e174` | `overlayfs: refresh image-owned init scripts on update` | A persistent `/etc` overlay previously could keep stale service launch scripts after an image update, silently defeating memory/runtime fixes. |
| `4831b0a` | `ustreamer: reduce camera streamer memory use` | Reduces always-on camera memory use without sacrificing the normal snapshot/live-view workflow. |
| `78ad740` | `overlayfs: escape shell expansions in preinit template` | Fixes rendering of the image-owned init-script cleanup in the pre-init template, allowing the update-path fix to build and execute correctly. |
| `b5d80fc` | `kernel: reduce runtime memory footprint on Centauri` | Removes unused kernel facilities and their runtime state from the appliance profile. |
| `4edb6be` | `python: reduce Klipper and Moonraker memory overhead` | Reduces Python code-object/cache and glibc allocator retention in the two largest long-lived user-space services. |
| `c25ea7b` | `kalico: bound input-shaper calibration memory` | Keeps Classic input-shaper processing from allocating FFT/window temporaries proportional to the complete accelerometer capture. |
| `c851dcb` | `rusty-shaper: add low-RAM input-shaper calibration` | Adds the validated rusty-shaper implementation as the default selectable, non-disruptive calibration path while retaining Classic as a fallback. |
| `51cda0e` | `calibration: skip stages with saved results` | Avoids unnecessary motion, heating, camera/UI disruption, and calibration-time memory pressure while retaining a deliberate full-recalibration path. |
| `6f900c9` | `kalico: persist input-shaper settings and stream raw accelerometer writes` | `SET_INPUT_SHAPER` now marks `[input_shaper]` dirty so `SAVE_CONFIG` persists rusty-shaper/Classic results; raw accelerometer captures are streamed to CSV instead of building a full samples list. |
| `b348004` | `calibration: detect only saved extruder PID results` | Prevents factory/default PID coefficients from being reported as user-calibrated. |

## Details

### Reliable zram and update behaviour

`b926d5d` replaces the previous one-shot zram setup with a bounded, idempotent initializer.  It waits for the device node/sysfs attributes, chooses the first available compressor, verifies that `/dev/zram0` is actually active in `/proc/swaps`, and retries transient failures once through a module reload.  It logs state and failures rather than silently continuing without swap.  The existing CC1 tuning remains (`swappiness=150`, 200% logical zram size, priority 100), but failure to bring swap online is now diagnosable.

`764e174` treats package-owned `/etc/init.d` scripts as release-owned before mounting the persistent `/etc` overlay.  On the first boot after an A/B update it removes only upper-layer copies or whiteouts that shadow a script present in the new image.  User-created scripts remain intact.  This is important for the Moonraker, uStreamer, and zram changes in this branch: old overlay copies can no longer leave a newly flashed image running an old service command. `78ad740` correctly escapes shell parameter expansions in the Python-rendered pre-init template, so this cleanup is build-safe and renders to the intended shell script.

### uStreamer: lower camera memory with live video retained

`4831b0a` keeps the production camera command at 864x480, camera-provided MJPEG, one worker/buffer, and 8 FPS:
```text
/usr/bin/ustreamer -r 864x480 -c HW -m MJPEG -b 1 -w 1 -f 8 -l \
  --host=0.0.0.0 --allow-origin=*
```

The patch caps shallow worker stacks, keeps a single newest HTTP JPEG rather than retaining stale frame copies, safely borrows camera JPEG data for HTTP delivery, drops the permanent blank RGB canvas, and starts generic frame buffers small enough to grow on demand.  It tries bounded USERPTR capture when supported and retries with MMAP when a UVC device rejects USERPTR; the deployed CC1 UVC camera was validated using the MMAP fallback.

With an active 864x480/8 FPS client on Centauri, uStreamer PSS fell from **4.67 MiB to 3.08 MiB** (1.59 MiB / 34% less) and RSS fell from **5.76 MiB to
4.14 MiB** (1.62 MiB / 28% less).  Snapshots and the live stream were verified
after a CC1 eMMC build and flash.

### Kernel and Python baseline reductions

`b5d80fc` adds the final CC1 kernel memory profile.  It disables unused debug and symbol tables, tracing/perf/task accounting, cgroups/container features, io_uring and other unused general-purpose interfaces, IPv6/firewall/bridge/ VLAN networking, and non-CC1 Allwinner pinctrl/PWM drivers.  It explicitly retains the interfaces required by the appliance: display/DRM, UVC media, RPMsg/remoteproc, GPIO/I2C/SPI, USB storage, swap, and zram.  The intent is less resident kernel code/state and fewer background accounting structures; this configuration change is not represented as a separate live MiB claim.

`4edb6be` starts Klipper and Moonraker with `-O -X no_debug_ranges`, ships target-version optimized bytecode without build-directory paths/debug ranges, and sets `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1` in both service environments.  The first two reduce Python code/cache overhead; the arena cap prevents glibc from retaining multiple per-thread heaps on a 128 MiB machine.  An isolated live Centauri test attributed approximately **3 MiB of Klipper PSS** reduction to the arena limit while the printer API remained healthy.  The change does not remove any Moonraker components or alter its public API.

### Bound Classic Kalico calibration allocations

`c25ea7b` changes Kalico's Welch PSD calculation to accumulate FFT energy in fixed 64-window batches rather than creating detrended/windowed/FFT arrays for all overlapping windows simultaneously.  It also retains accelerometer data as `float32` and uses timestamps relative to the first sample before packing. The raw capture CSV contract and PSD calculation are preserved, while the largest temporary arrays are bounded by batch size instead of capture length. This makes Classic calibration safer under memory pressure even when rusty-shaper is not selected.

### rusty-shaper: faster, lower-pressure calibration with equal output

`c851dcb` packages the stripped GPL-3 rusty-shaper binary and its fully checksummed Cargo dependencies, then integrates it

Adds a new CSS code `[[390,82,39]]` to the leaderboard, constructed as a **generalized bicycle (2BGA)** code on the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_{195}$.

- **Construction:** circulant size $195$; $a(x)$ and $b(x)$ each have weight $16$ and are both multiples of a degree-$41$ divisor $g$ of $x^{195}-1$, giving $k = 82$.

## Motivation

This pull request addresses two key areas to improve robustness and developer experience:

1. **Fixing `ui_element` Registry Collisions:**  
   Previously, it was possible for multiple input classes to silently register the same `ui_element` string, leading to ambiguous or incorrect widget rendering (e.g., `ui_element="hidden"`, `"date"`, `"number"`, or `"range"` could resolve unpredictably). This PR ensures the registry now rejects duplicate `ui_element` assignments, enforcing a strict one-to-one mapping. This guarantees that every `ui_element` value in the documentation or code resolves to exactly one component, eliminating subtle UI bugs and making the system more predictable and maintainable.

2. **Expanding AI Assistant Documentation with a Verified Example:**  
   The AI instructions and docs are enhanced with a complete, end-to-end tested example and an authoritative, automatically verified table of all supported `ui_element` values. This removes ambiguity for language model integrations and ensures that documentation, code, and registry remain in sync. The new test (`test_authoritative_ui_element_table_matches_registry`) fails if the docs and registry diverge, enforcing documentation accuracy and preventing future regressions.

## Why this improves the project

- **Reliability:** Enforcing unique `ui_element` mappings prevents hard-to-diagnose UI bugs and ensures consistent rendering for all field types.
- **Documentation Accuracy:** The AI assistant docs are now guaranteed to match the code. Integrators and developers will always have an up-to-date, verified reference of valid `ui_element` values and examples.
- **Test Coverage:** The new test increases confidence in both code and docs by catching mismatches early.
- **Developer Experience:** The improved examples, clearer file structure references, and explicit FastAPI composition patterns make it easier for new users to understand and extend the project.

---

**Summary:**  
This PR tightens input widget registration to prevent collisions and raises the bar for documentation quality by making all `ui_element` references authoritative and test-verified. This leads to more robust forms and a better developer/onboarding experience.

body:
Implements Track A of `.claude/plans/2026-07-19-AIProxy.spec.md` (Codex/WHAM + subscription hardening), including all optional items, with live verification on the owner machine.

## Phases

**P1 — Usage correctness**
- `extractLatestUsageFromSse` reads nested `response.usage` from Responses `response.completed` events (WHAM shape), not just top-level.
- Chat JSON + stream paths assert usage survival end-to-end.
- `getUsage` for `openai-subscription` reports **proxy-observed** today/30d counts from the local store + plan tier from the JWT — never claims ChatGPT plan quota.
- **P1.4 estimate fallback:** when upstream omits usage on a successful exchange, a char-heuristic estimate is recorded, tagged `usage.source: "estimated"` (+ `estimated_requests` daily counter, shown in `usage` output). Never presented as upstream numbers.

**P2 — Resilience**
- Non-OK WHAM responses map to OpenAI-shaped envelopes (`authentication_error` / `rate_limit_error` / `upstream_error`) with actionable copy.
- Per-account in-memory cooldown on 429 (honours `Retry-After`, else exponential backoff 30s→10min); unhealthy accounts cool 15 min.
- 401 → one forced token refresh (rotation-safe under the AI-config lock) + one retry; second 401 marks the account unhealthy.
- `openaiSub.failoverAccountNames`: additional `openai-sub` accounts tried in order within the same request.

**P3 — Auth UX**
- `tools ai-proxy accounts login codex` — PKCE browser flow, persists an `openai-sub` AI-config account and points/creates a proxy account at it.
- `tools ai-proxy accounts status` — auth source (ai-config vs codex-auth.json), token expiry, ChatGPT plan.
- README rewritten for the codex provider.

**P4 — Parameter fidelity (probe-backed)**
- **Live probe matrix (2026-07-19, Plus plan)** documented in the spec: `max_output_tokens`/`temperature`/`top_p`/`previous_response_id` all 400 "Unsupported parameter"; `store` must stay `false`; omitting `reasoning` and `effort: medium` both accepted.
- Dropped params recorded and surfaced via `x-ai-proxy-dropped` response header (propagated through the chat translation path too — found in live smoke) + once-per-process warn.
- Client `reasoning` passes through (unknown efforts clamp to `low`); `openaiSub.defaultReasoningEffort` config (`"none"` omits — probe-validated).

**P5 — Catalog**
- Aliases: builtin `latest`/`codex`/`mini` + per-account `openaiSub.aliases`, advertised in the catalog when resolvable.
- `models` table gains MODAL column (input modalities); context window + parallel-tool metadata carried on `ProxyModelMeta`.
- Image input to a model that provably lacks the image modality → 400 `unsupported_modality` naming vision-capable models (unknown modalities pass through).

**P6 — Translation edges**
- Chat `image_url` parts → Responses `input_image` (detail preserved).
- Non-function tool types stripped + recorded (WHAM accepts flat function tools only).
- `response.failed` → structured error envelope with upstream code.

**P7 — Observability**
- Structured request log fields (servedBy, reasoningEffort, dropped, authSource, elapsedMs…).
- `usage --provider <type> --breakdown` per-model 30d aggregates.
- `AI_PROXY_DEBUG_CAPTURE=1` saves the last failing upstream exchange (redacted — no tokens) under `~/.genesis-tools/ai-proxy/debug/`.

**P8 — resolved impossible:** WHAM rejects `store:true` ("Store must be set to false") and `previous_response_id` ("Unsupported parameter") — probed live. `store:false` stays forced; both recorded as dropped when clients send them.

**Track B** — design doc only (`.claude/plans/2026-07-19-AIProxy-TrackB-design.md`); build stays gated on demand.

Also carried on this branch: `feat(loc)` — user's concurrent loc-tool improvements (binary-file skip, expanded language catalog), split into its own commit.

## Verification

- 173 ai-proxy tests + openai-utils/loc suites green (`bun test`), `tsgo --noEmit` clean on every commit (pre-commit CI mirror).
- **Live WHAM probes** (9 controlled requests, Plus plan) — results table in spec §4.

  - non-stream chat: 200, `CODEX_OK`, upstream usage `13/18/31`, `x-ai-proxy-dropped: max_tokens` header present;
  - streamed alias `codex/codex/latest`: 200 with usage in stream;

- `accounts status` live: shows `codex (plus)`, source `~/.codex/auth.json`, expiry.

Not verified here: end-to-end browser login flow, failover with two real accounts, Cursor agent tool round-trip.

body:
A hand-off document to give to an agent working in the **DJL ExecuTorch engine** repo, covering the two items that came out of the Windows static-CRT work.

`docs/handover-to-engine.md` already exists, but it is a *cold-start* doc covering the whole C1–C9 contract and its §1 still names an old release tag. Rather than grow it further, this adds a focused work order for a reader who already has the engine context and needs only the action items.

## Stream A — adopt `windows-x86_64-static`

Select the `-static` pin row on Windows, compile every target linked into the JNI DLL `/MT` to match, and verify empirically. Includes the two `dumpbin` traps that cost real debugging time here (the MSYS `/nologo` path-conversion failure, and why the check must assert on the *presence* of the expected marker), plus proving on a clean image that no VC++ redistributable is actually needed — which is the user-facing claim.

Carries the measured warning that a `/MD` consumer links a `/MT` artifact with **no error and no LNK4098**, so a clean link is not evidence.

## Stream B — C++17 propagation check

ExecuTorch does not export its C++17 requirement via `INTERFACE_COMPILE_FEATURES`. Framed honestly as an investigation that may correctly conclude "nothing to change" — since the guard is `#error`, a building engine is already getting C++17 from somewhere, and the real question is *where from, and how fragile is that*.

Explicitly tells the engine agent **not** to file upstream against `pytorch/executorch` — that item is held here pending the next ET release.

## Note

Deliberately contains **no release tag, URL or SHA256**. It instructs the reader to resolve the latest release and take `EtRuntimePin.cmake` from it, which is the C6 source of truth. Verified with a grep that no version leaked in.

Docs only — no code, no CI changes.

### Motivation

Closes #127. §3.2 elite-share row — the second edge on the owners' row.

## The double edge
Under H1 the owners' row **ratcheted up structurally** and fell **only on catastrophe** (a won revolt burning the charters, a refinery collapse, a plague). B5 gives it an ordinary downward edge: **where the market reaches, competition bids concentrated rents down and the owners capture less of every gain.** A wired, central hub does not hold a monopoly the way an isolated valley does; a boom mints new owners (rank churn without collapse); and a police state freezes both.

## The mechanic
- **`rentKeep = 1 − 0.85·marketAccess`** (market access = central AND on the grid) now scales BOTH the rent-capture ratchet (toll house, works, seam, aerie) AND the owners' share of the town's **wealth upswing** — the boom is bid toward labor where rivals compete for it, though the owners still bear the whole of a bust.
- A standing **competition** decay eats at high concentration where access is high; **boom-churn** mints new owners.
- A **police state freezes it all** (`occupied` proxy until B9's order axis).

## "Without a catastrophe" — the honest measure
A refinery collapse is a **universal endgame** (extraction always depletes, the works always eventually go dark), so no full-length world is literally event-free. Rather than pin an absurd short/tiny corner, the fall is measured on the **ordinary component**: new `elite_ordinary_delta` (per region) / `elite_ordinary_mean` (findings) read the row's move since founding with every catastrophe shock **charged out** (won-revolt −25, collapse −10, plague −8, crushed-revolt +10 all removed). author: tejitpabari99
body:
## What

Hardens the Windows autostart flow to avoid EDR false-positives and cleans up local developer experience.

Four commits, all on this branch:

1. **`feat(autostart)`** — Replace the `reg.exe` shell-out in `src/autostart/win32.ts` with direct `RegSetValueExW` calls via the `registry-js` native module. Callers untouched (public API preserved).
2. **`docs`** — Add a troubleshooting entry for `ERR_SSL_SSL/TLS_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE` on `npm install` (corp TLS-inspecting proxy is the usual culprit).
3. **`test`** — Gate the 2 real-registry autostart tests behind `process.env.CI` so local `npm test` no longer writes to `HKCU\...\Run`. GitHub Actions runs them (CI=true auto-set); developers can opt-in with `CRONTICK_RUN_REGISTRY_TESTS=1`.
4. **`chore`** — Patch changeset for 0.1.1.

## Why

- Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (and most EDRs) flag the literal command line `reg add HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run ...` as a persistence IOC (MITRE T1547.001). Calling `RegSetValueExW` from `node.exe` directly skips the `cmd.exe → reg.exe` chain and the alert pattern.
- Running `npm test` locally was writing scratch registry values every time, which triggered CDI alerts on corp-managed devices. Gating those to CI-only fixes that without losing coverage.
- The SSL troubleshooting doc is a common-ish install gotcha on corp networks; capturing it in docs saves the next user an evening.

## How

- Added `registry-js` (`^1.16.0`) to `optionalDependencies` (Windows prebuilds; no-op on Linux/Mac).
- Rewrote `install`/`remove`/`status` in `src/autostart/win32.ts` to use `setValue`/`deleteValue`/`enumerateValues`. VBS shim writing is unchanged.
- Swapped test mocks from `child_process.spawn` to `registry-js` in `tests/autostart.test.ts`.
- Wrapped real-registry tests in `tests/api.autostart.test.ts` and `tests/mcp.autostart.test.ts` with `describe.skipIf(...)`.
- Documented the changes in `docs/security.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `docs/getting-started.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`.

## Testing

- `npm test` (CI=true): **241 passed, 0 skipped**
- `npm test` (no CI): **239 passed, 2 skipped** (the gated real-registry tests)
- `reg query` before/after `npm test` (no CI): **zero registry changes**
- `npm run lint`: clean (existing warnings only)
- `npm run build`: clean; `registry-js` correctly externalized
- `node scripts/verify-tarball.mjs`: passes

## Version

Patch bump to `0.1.1`. Changeset in `.changeset/registry-js-autostart.md` — the changesets bot will open a Version Packages PR after this merges.

## Notes

- No user-facing API change.
- End users doing `npm install -g crontick` and `crontick daemon start` will never touch the registry. Only `crontick autostart install` writes to `HKCU\...\Run`, and now it does so via the Win32 API rather than `reg.exe`.

...
[docs/ONBOARDING.md] — already in sync ✓
...

body:
Campaign #2 of the defaults programme (#256). Closes the **12 INERT** mismatches, and fixes a bug found while investigating `baseflow_scalar`.

## Inertness was proven, not asserted

Every one of the 12 was independently re-verified by grepping each read: 5 have **zero** reads (`nsegspc`, `nyr_forcing`, `h2osno_max`, `n_dom_pfts`, `downscale_hillslope_meteorology`), and the rest sit behind `> 0` / `> 0.0` guards that reject the old and new values identically.

Then it was demonstrated empirically. With all 12 flipped, the full suite moved by **exactly the 12 pin assertions and nothing else**:

```
baseline:  26150 pass +  0 fail + 3 broken = 26153
flipped:   26140 pass + 12 fail + 3 broken = 26155
           −10 pass / +12 fail  →  precisely the 12 pins
           +2 total             →  the new calibration regression test
```

**Zero physics assertions moved.** The pins are now closed to the correct values — which is what #256 required, having warned that pinning known-wrong values risks calcifying them into "expected".

Notable: `h2osno_max` was `-999.0`, and `controlMod.F90:557` **hard-errors on `<= 0`** — a value CTSM refuses to start on. It was harmless here only because this `varctl` copy is a dead duplicate; the physics reads `varcon.H2OSNO_MAX`.

## Side-finding: two calibration parameters had never worked

`_apply_baseflow_scalar!` and `_apply_fff!` each set the override correctly and then looped over `inst.column.baseflow_scalar` / `.fff` — **fields `ColumnData` does not have**. Both threw `FieldError` on their *first* call, so neither hydrology calibration parameter had ever been applied.

It survived because `test_calibration.jl` asserted only `.name` and never invoked `apply!` — a vacuous check, the same class swept in #255/#257. The dead loops are removed (the override above them is the live mechanism, read by `clm_run!`), and the test now **calls `apply!` and asserts the override lands**, so it cannot regress behind another name-only assertion. 30/30.

## Deliberately NOT changed
- **`baseflow_scalar`'s 10× value.** Repairing the applier makes the driver-vs-calibration disagreement genuinely live for the first time; that needs its own validated campaign.
- **The 8 `use_cn`-conditional flags.** Setting e.g. `use_flexibleCN = true` while every consumer defaults `false` would make the control state advertise a configuration the port does not run — a worse landmine than the honest `false`.

author: jharvieux
body:
## What & why

`pnpm dynamic-validate <t> --execute` self-provisioned a local Supabase using the target workdir as the project-id on Supabase's **default ports/volume names**, and its teardown was workdir-scoped. A prior run (cipherx recall) deleted two pre-existing local-dev volumes belonging to another project (`supabase_db_atc-main`, `supabase_storage_atc-main`). This is a prerequisite for the ATC pass, which must not touch non-ATC local projects.

## The fix (`src/pentest/live-standup.ts`)

- **Unique, run-scoped project-id + non-default ports.** Each run provisions under `harvey-dv-<hash-of-target+time>` on a 10-wide non-default port window, inside an **isolated temp workdir we own** — Supabase is never pointed at the client's own `supabase/` dir (its `config.toml`/ports/seed are exactly what collided). The client's migrations are copied into our isolated project; a fresh `config.toml` is stamped with our project-id + remapped ports. Overridable via `HARVEY_DV_PROJECT` / `HARVEY_DV_PORT_BASE`. Two concurrent runs get different project-ids and port windows.
- **Scoped teardown.** `supabase stop --project-id <id> --no-backup` (scoped, never a blanket removal), plus a defense-in-depth pass that removes only docker volumes whose name ends in `_<projectId>`. A foreign `supabase_db_<other>` can never match.
- **Fail loud, never clobber.** A preflight refuses to start if the api/db port is already in use or a docker volume already carries the run's project-id.

## Tests (`src/pentest/live-standup.test.ts`)

New unit tests assert: two runs get distinct project-ids; the port window is non-default, internally distinct, and differs between runs; `config.toml` is rewritten with the unique id + remapped ports (comments untouched); and a teardown seam that records removed volumes proves a pre-existing foreign `supabase_db_atc-main` / `supabase_db_other` is **left untouched** while only the run's own volumes are removed.

## Live validation

Ran `dynamic-validate --execute` against a small two-tenant target after `docker volume create supabase_db_isolationtest`:
- Provisioned under `harvey-dv-efa6476dd3` on ports api=54931 db=54932 (non-default), stood up, seeded two tenants, ran the PostgREST matrix, wrote `M2.pass.json`.
- **After teardown: `supabase_db_isolationtest` survived**; the run's own containers/volumes were fully removed; no leftovers. Threw-away volume then removed by hand — final docker state has no stray supabase volumes.

`pnpm verify` green (1689 tests, knip clean).

Closes #604

body:
## Summary

- add a stable-Rust checksum backend with runtime-dispatched ARM64 NEON and x86-64 AVX2 implementations
- retain an algebraically equivalent scalar fallback for unsupported CPUs and architectures
- keep unsafe code isolated to the checksum backend with documented safety invariants
- remove the desktop discovery-stage file read so new mail is read and decoded only once by the upload stage

## Why

Checksum validation previously processed one byte at a time, limiting instruction-level parallelism. Desktop discovery also read and validated each new file before the upload stage read and decoded the same file again.

This keeps the checksum and decoded output unchanged while reducing CPU work and eliminating the duplicate local file read.

## Local performance

Measured with seven-run stable release medians using the existing `opt-level = "z"` profile.

### Round 1 — initial local cache

| Workload | Before | After | Improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Checksum validation across 2,012 files (20.70 MB) | 15.439 ms | 5.115 ms | 66.9% |
| Full decode across 2,012 files | 108.955 ms | 96.422 ms | 11.5% |

The cache contained 1,989 files at or below 100 KB. On that subset, SIMD reduced median full-decode time by another 2.3% compared with the optimized scalar fallback, with no small-file regression.

### Round 2 — expanded local cache

The expanded workload contained 18,262 decodable files (45.12 MB), including 18,239 files at or below 100 KB.

| Workload | Original | Optimized scalar | SIMD | Original → SIMD |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Checksum validation | 30.905 ms | 14.986 ms | 9.989 ms | 67.7% |
| Full decode | 213.338 ms | 197.369 ms | 191.281 ms | 10.3% |

On this ARM64 system, runtime-dispatched NEON improved checksum validation by another 33.3% over the optimized scalar fallback and improved full decoding by another 3.1%.

### Round 3 — additional local cache

The third workload contained 7,247 decodable files (15.50 MB), including 7,241 files at or below 100 KB.

| Workload | Original | Optimized scalar | SIMD | Original → SIMD |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Checksum validation | 10.460 ms | 5.138 ms | 3.448 ms | 67.0% |
| Full decode | 69.236 ms | 64.001 ms | 62.133 ms | 10.3% |

On the same ARM64 system, runtime-dispatched NEON improved checksum validation by another 32.9% over the optimized scalar fallback and improved full decoding by another 2.9%. Across all three datasets, the optimized implementation consistently reduces checksum time by about 67% and full-decode time by about 10–12%.

## Compatibility

- ARM64 uses NEON after runtime feature detection.
- x86-64 uses AVX2 after runtime feature detection.
- Other targets and CPUs use the portable scalar implementation.
- The primary decoder crate continues to forbid unsafe code.
- Decoded and processed document output is unchanged.

## Validation

body:
## Summary

Adds an embeddable **workspace File browser** to `LmStreaming.Sample` — a modal opened from the chat header that lists, navigates, previews, downloads, uploads, and deletes files in the active conversation's sandbox workspace. Implements the frozen, spec-reviewed acceptance criteria in #195 (BOT-PLAN v3, Revobot verdict: *READY*).

Fixes #195

## What's included

**SDK (`src/Sandbox`)** — additive, no breaking changes
- `SandboxDirectoryEntry` + `SandboxEntryType { File, Directory, Symlink }`
- `ListDirectoryEntriesAsync` (rich name/type/size/nameLossy), `ReadFileBytesAsync` (raw, caller byte cap), `WriteFileBytesAsync` (raw); `ListDirectoryAsync`'s `IReadOnlyList<string>` signature is **unchanged** (existing `CodeReviewDaemon.Sample` consumer keeps compiling). A shared page-iterator is extracted from `ListDirectoryAsync`.
- Optional `maxBytes` threaded through the capped-download seam (clamped to the 64 MiB ceiling); `SandboxException.IsDirectReadCapExceeded` typed over-cap signal.

**Session resolution (`src/LmAgentInfra`)**
- A dedicated per-thread `SandboxEstablishedBinding` (workspace ref + creating credential) is the only "this conversation has a sandbox" signal — separate from `_sessionThreads` membership and the pool's `AgentEntry`.
- `ResolveThreadWorkspaceSessionAsync` is **non-creating**: no binding ⇒ `NoSession` with zero gateway calls; present ⇒ credential-conflict gate then live-resolve/recreate on the binding's identity.
- The pool publishes the staged binding **only on a successful agent-entry commit under the per-thread lock**, and clears it (compare-and-clear under the same lock) on removal.

**Controller + wiring (`samples/LmStreaming.Sample`)**
- `FileBrowserController` (`api/conversations/{threadId}/files`, `[InboundS2SAuth]`): component-wise authoritative path resolution (exactly one non-lossy ordinal match per level, server-returned type; client type/lossy/session never trusted); download (attachment + nosniff, 64 MiB, 413 no-truncation); preview (server allowlist, 256 KiB/5000-line caps, strict UTF-8); upload (one request/file, inclusive 64 MiB on declared **and** observed, basename validation); delete via `rm`/`rm -r --` assembled from the server type; no-session ⇒ 200 listing / 409 actions; gateway-unavailable ⇒ 503.
- `Program.cs` stages the binding in the workspace-agent factory, wires the pool binding sink, and raises the Kestrel/FormOptions upload ceiling.

**Client (`ClientApp`)**
- Shared `BaseModal` (role=dialog/aria-modal/labelled, focus trap + restore, Escape); `FileBrowser.vue` (breadcrumbs, symlink non-nav, lossy non-actionable, inline `<pre>` preview, download, delete-confirm, picker + drag-drop, 500-row "more" notice, active-workspace display, advisory overwrite-confirm); `FileBrowserModal.vue`; hand-rolled `fileBrowserApi.ts` + `useFileBrowser.ts`; a gated "Files" header button in `ChatLayout.vue`.

## Key Decisions

1. **Session resolution keys on a dedicated transactional binding, not pool/thread membership.** `RegisterThread` is gated on sub-agent options, so it isn't a reliable "sandbox established" signal; the binding is published atomically with the `AgentEntry` commit under the per-thread lock (and compare-and-cleared on removal), so a concurrent remove+recreate can't strand it.
2. **Non-creating resolution — the browser never provisions a sandbox.** No binding (including a live pooled agent from a non-sandbox mode, or a shared `(workspaceId, appId)` session another conversation owns) ⇒ `NoSessionYet` with zero create calls. Recreation-after-eviction reuses the binding's frozen identity; cross-process-restart is out of scope.
3. **Paths are resolved component-by-component against the gateway's authoritative listing** (one non-lossy ordinal match per level, server-returned type), so client-supplied type/lossy/workspace/session inputs are never trusted; delete is composed from the server type via the existing `ExecuteAsync` — no new gateway/SDK delete primitive.
4. **Preview renders via an inline `<pre>`, not `CodeBlockRich`** — reconnaissance showed `CodeBlockRich` is coupled to the tool-call render pipeline (`{ view: ToolPillView; toolCall: ToolCall }`); fabricating a synthetic tool view for a file preview would be fragile. The AC ("CodeBlockRich-*style* rendering") is satisfied by the equivalent styled `<pre>`. (Only documented deviation.)
5. **Self-review (4 independent reviewers) surfaced only MEDIUM/LOW findings, all fixed** — 503-on-gateway-unavailable mapping, the binding-clear race, a typed over-cap signal (replacing a brittle message-match), and client UX (surfaced per-file upload failures, Escape-scoping, deferred URL revoke).

## Verification

- `dotnet build` (analyzer-clean) + `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` clean.
- **Sandbox.Tests: 224** (net8.0 + net9.0) · **LmStreaming.Sample.Tests: 725 / 1 skip / 0 fail** · **ClientApp vitest: 509** + `vue-tsc` clean · **Browser E2E FileBrowserTests: 1/1**.
- New coverage maps every v3 acceptance-test group: rich-listing/protocol mapping, raw read/write + `maxBytes` caps, transactional binding (publish/clear/failed-switch), non-creating resolver outcomes, component-wise lossy/ambiguous rejection, download attachment+nosniff + over-cap 413, preview zero-read/post-read/line-cap/UTF-8 determinism, upload declared+observed cap + basename + target_busy + mixed outcomes + overwrite-confirm, delete argv per server type + exit code, and modal a11y.

author: chuenchen309
body:
## The issue

`BaseCache._fetch` is typed `(start: int | None, end: int | None)`, and most cache implementations treat `end=None` as "read to the end of the file":

- `ReadAheadCache`: `if end is None or end > self.size: end = self.size`
- `BytesCache`: `if end is None: end = self.size`
- `BlockCache` / `MMapCache`: handle it too

`FirstChunkCache` is the odd one out — it does `end = min(end, self.size)`, which raises `TypeError` on `None`:

```python
>>> from fsspec.caching import FirstChunkCache
>>> c = FirstChunkCache(4, lambda s, e: b"x" * (e - s), 100)
>>> c._fetch(0, None)
TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'NoneType'
```

## Fix

Fall back to `self.size` when `end is None`, mirroring the sibling caches. One-line behavioural change; the existing `int` path is untouched.

## Scope / reachability

I want to be upfront: the buffered-read path (`AbstractBufferedFile.read`) resolves the length to an `int` before calling `self.cache._fetch`, so a normal file read doesn't hit this. But `_fetch` is a public contract that the other caches honor — the shared `test_cache_getitem` already exercises `_fetch(None, 4)` (start=None) across every cache — and `FirstChunkCache` is the only subclass that diverges. This makes it consistent.

## Verification

- Extended the existing parametrized `test_cache_getitem` with a `_fetch(0, None)` assertion. It fails only for `FirstChunkCache[first]` on `main` (TypeError) and passes for all caches with this change.
- `fsspec/tests/test_caches.py`: **147 passed**.
- `ruff check` clean.

The human account holder reviews every change and is accountable for it. The verification above is real and re-runnable from the diff.
